title: New Case Filed Against Political Prisoner Mostafa Tajzadeh
content:
According to HRANA, citing Emtedad, a new case has been filed against Mostafa Tajzadeh while he is in prison.

Fakhrossadat Mohtashamipour, Tajzadeh’s wife, stated that after his furlough was approved and the administrative procedures were completed, the process of sending him on furlough was halted at the final stage. Follow-up inquiries revealed that a new case had been opened against him on the charge of “propaganda against the regime,” with bail set at 500 million tomans.

According to his wife, the case dates back to August of this year and must be resolved by the branch handling the case.

Mostafa Tajzadeh was arrested by security forces on July 8, 2022, and subsequently transferred to Evin Prison.

Tajzadeh has faced several judicial cases in recent years.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Emtedad, a new case has been filed against Mostafa Tajzadeh while he is in prison.

title: Yaser Hosseini and Mohsen Asadi Arrested in Kamyaran
content:
According to HRANA, citing Kurdpa, Yaser Hosseini and Mohsen Asadi were arrested in Kamyaran.

According to the report, the two Kamyaran residents were arrested separately by security forces at their workplaces on Thursday, September 17, without the presentation of a judicial warrant.

As of the time of this report, no information has been obtained regarding the reasons for their arrests, their place of detention, or the charges brought against Yaser Hosseini and Mohsen Asadi.

Yaser Hosseini and Mohsen Asadi have both previously been arrested in connection with their activities.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Kurdpa, Yaser Hosseini and Mohsen Asadi were arrested in Kamyaran.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Woman Executed at Dastgerd Prison in Isfahan
content:
According to HRANA, a prisoner was executed at Dastgerd Prison in Isfahan at dawn on Monday, September 14, 2026.

HRANA has identified the prisoner as Rezvan Asgharzadeh, a 45-year-old mother of six. On Sunday evening, one day before her execution, she was transferred from Dowlatabad Prison in Isfahan to Dastgerd Prison.

According to information received by HRANA, Asgharzadeh was arrested approximately six years and six months ago in connection with drug-related offenses. About two years ago, Branch 5 of the Isfahan Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Hemmat-Nejad, sentenced her to death. The sentence was subsequently upheld by the Supreme Court.

An informed source close to her family told HRANA: “During her imprisonment, Ms. Asgharzadeh memorized several sections of the Quran in hopes of qualifying for clemency, and until her final days she remained hopeful that her sentence would be commuted. Her name was initially included on the list of prisoners eligible for clemency. However, following a negative report submitted by Fatemeh Asgarian, the head of Dowlatabad Prison in Isfahan, her name was removed from the list.”
snippet: According to HRANA, a prisoner was executed at Dastgerd Prison in Isfahan at dawn on Monday, September 14, 2026.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Hossein Molaei Sentenced to 15 Years in Prison
content:
According to HRANA, Hossein Molaei has been sentenced to imprisonment.

Based on information received by HRANA, Molaei, who is currently held in Greater Tehran Prison, was sentenced by Branch 29 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court to 15 years in prison on the charge of “supporting Israel.”

An informed source familiar with his situation told HRANA: “Mr. Molaei is in a difficult financial situation and cannot afford the cost of an attorney. Accordingly, he needs access to legal counsel to pursue the judicial proceedings in his case and appeal the sentence issued against him.”

Hossein Molaei, 50, was arrested by security forces in March 2026 and transferred to Greater Tehran Prison.

HRANA is reviewing details regarding the specific acts underlying the charge brought against him.
snippet: According to HRANA, Hossein Molaei has been sentenced to imprisonment.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Merchants and Shopkeepers Strike in Several Cities on Fourth Anniversary of Mahsa Amini’s Death
content:
According to HRANA, yesterdam, September 16, 2026, merchants and shopkeepers in Sanandaj, Saqqez, Mahabad, Baneh, Bukan, Divandarreh, Oshnavieh, Piranshahr, and Qorveh went on strike.

Kurdpa, which covers human rights violations in Kurdish regions, also reported strikes by merchants and shopkeepers in Kermanshah, Urmia, Kamyaran, and Marivan.

Reports received by HRANA indicate that security forces established a heavy presence throughout Saqqez, creating a heightened security atmosphere. By blocking the main and secondary roads leading to Aichi Cemetery, they prevented Amini’s family and other citizens from visiting her grave.

title: Nasser Bahmanyari Arrested in Karaj
content:
According to HRANA, Nasser Bahmanyari was arrested in Karaj.

According to information received by HRANA, the arrest took place on Tuesday, September 15, when agents of the IRGC Intelligence Organization apprehended him at his private residence in Karaj.

An informed source close to his family confirmed the news to HRANA and said: “Mr. Bahmanyari was arrested due to his activities and positions of protest.”

As of the time of this report, no information has been obtained regarding the reasons for his arrest, his place of detention, or the charges brought against him.

Nasser Bahmanyari, 67, has previously faced judicial action due to his activities. Following his arrest in Yasuj in 1999, he was dismissed from his teaching position with the Ministry of Education.
snippet: According to HRANA, Nasser Bahmanyari was arrested in Karaj.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Amin Shirafkan and Alireza Hajatmand Arrested in Gorgan
content:
According to HRANA, Amin (Mazdak) Shirafkan and Alireza Hajatmand were arrested in Gorgan.

An informed source close to the families of the two individuals confirmed the news to HRANA and said: “On Wednesday, September 16, officers from the Public Security and Intelligence Police went to Mr. Shirafkan’s workplace, located in the Shirangi Passage in Gorgan, and arrested him along with his shop assistant, identified as Alireza Hajatmand. They were subsequently transferred to a detention facility operated by the Criminal Investigation Police.”

As of the time of this report, no information has been obtained regarding the reasons for their arrests or the charges brought against them.

Amin Shirafkan is 48 years old, while Alireza Hajatmand is 20 and is from the city of Aq Qala. Of the two, Amin (Mazdak) Shirafkan has previously been arrested and received judicial convictions in connection with his activities.
snippet: According to HRANA, Amin (Mazdak) Shirafkan and Alireza Hajatmand were arrested in Gorgan.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Report on the Latest Status of Detained Sunni Citizens in Ahvaz
content:
According to HRANA, 10 Sunni citizens in Ahvaz, including Majid Sharifi (Savari), Arkan Sharifi (Savari), 17, Razi Heydari, Hossein Heydari, Abdolhadi Asakereh, Lafteh Heydari, Hamzeh Sayahi, and Mohammad Savari, remain in detention.

According to information received by HRANA, Majid Sharifi (Savari), 44, remains held at the Ministry of Intelligence’s detention facility in Ahvaz. The other seven identified detainees have been transferred to the quarantine ward of Sheiban Prison in Ahvaz. Majid Sharifi suffers from kidney failure, and reports received by HRANA indicate that he is in poor physical condition. Given his underlying medical condition, his continued detention at the Ministry of Intelligence’s detention facility has raised concerns among his relatives about his health.

These citizens were arrested on September 4, 2026, by Ministry of Intelligence agents at Majid Sharifi’s home in the Kuy-e Mashali neighborhood of Ahvaz. The arrests were carried out without the presentation of a judicial warrant and were accompanied by physical violence.

title: Rahim Molaeian Sentenced to Prison by Revolutionary Court
content:
According to HRANA, Rahim Molaeian has been sentenced to prison.

Under a ruling issued on Sunday, September 13, by Branch 1 of the Babol Revolutionary Court, Mr. Molaeian was sentenced to six months in prison on the charge of “propaganda against the regime.”

According to information received by HRANA, Molaeian’s paintings and posts he shared as Instagram Stories were cited as evidence supporting the charge against him.

A hearing on the charge was held before the same branch on September 6 of this year.

In April-May of this year, his office, studio, and residence were searched by 12 security agents, and 28 of Molaeian’s paintings were confiscated for 48 hours. In connection with the case, Mr. Molaeian was also interrogated by security agencies on three occasions, with each session lasting four hours.

Rahim Molaeian, 66, is a painter and sculptor from Babol, where he currently resides. He is married and the father of three children.
snippet: According to HRANA, Rahim Molaeian has been sentenced to prison.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Najmeh Amini from Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad: “I Have Been Sentenced to Death”
content:
According to HRANA, one of those arrested during last year’s January protests, has reported that she has been sentenced to death.

In an audio message from Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad, Ms. Amini stated that the judiciary issued her death sentence on September 16, 2026.

The prisoner has called on the United Nations, lawyers, activists, and human rights organizations to review her case so that she may exercise her right to a fair trial.

HRANA is unable to independently verify Najmeh Amini’s statements.

A court hearing to address the charges against Ms. Amini was held in August of this year at the Mashhad Revolutionary Court. She was tried on charges of “assembly and collusion against national security” and “insulting sacred beliefs and the Imams.”

On January 31, 2026, Najmeh Amini was arrested by security forces at Ferdowsi Shopping Center in Mashhad during the January protests. She was subsequently transferred to Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad.

Najmeh Amini, 23, is an accounting student and a resident of Mashhad.
snippet: According to HRANA, one of those arrested during last year’s January protests, has reported that she has been sentenced to death.
